historyReviewBoundary: All 115 histories have author source checks. Final independent review covered metadata and numerical checks for all 115 classes, 12 deeper class targets and source-gap samples in seven classes. It did not independently verify every passage of every cited source.

history.name: 5-HT3 receptor antagonists

starting.description: Clinical and experimental antiemetic effects of metoclopramide, and ferret responses to renzapride versus a dopamine antagonist, prompted investigation of a non-dopaminergic mechanism. Separately, a Glaxo migraine pilot's reported nausea relief and metoclopramide's high-dose effectiveness prompted work on ondansetron as an antiemetic.

inspiration.description: Observed antiemetic effects of synthetic metoclopramide and renzapride, reported nausea relief with ondansetron in a migraine pilot, serotonin-related responses, and cocaine as a separate pharmacological and chemical starting point for the MDL72222 experimental tool; no cocaine-to-ondansetron molecular ancestry is established.

steps.description: High-dose metoclopramide reduced chemotherapy-associated emesis, motivating investigation beyond dopamine antagonism.
In a separate chemical and pharmacological branch, cocaine and related molecules supplied a starting point for MDL72222, made for a migraine research program rather than initially as an antiemetic.

Renzapride suppressed cisplatin vomiting without D2 antagonism; researchers used MDL72222 to test whether a selective serotonin-receptor antagonist was antiemetic. In the 1986 test it reduced cisplatin-induced vomiting in ferrets.

In Glaxo's parallel route, an uncontrolled 1985 ondansetron migraine pilot reportedly relieved nausea and vomiting in some patients; together with metoclopramide evidence this led Tyers to pursue a 5-HT3 antiemetic hypothesis, followed by animal and clinical development.
Glaxo's 1988 pharmacological experiments characterized ondansetron (GR38032F) as a selective 5-HT3 antagonist, and the retrospective reports subsequent U.S. registration in 1991.

design.description: Researchers synthesized the selective MDL72222 antagonist using a cocaine template and deliberately tested it after antiemetic observations. Separately, Glaxo synthesized ondansetron, characterized its selective receptor antagonism and developed it for antiemetic use. The MDL72222 template is not a proven chemical lineage for ondansetron, whose detailed design route is not established here.

circumstances.description: The follow-up experiment with the selective antagonist was planned to probe competing mechanisms; this does not characterize every earlier discovery as planned or unexpected.

limits: The cocaine-to-MDL72222 branch is not established as the chemical ancestry of ondansetron.
The Beecham and Glaxo lines both used observations, but sources do not establish that either company initiated the other's work. The 1985 Glaxo migraine pilot was uncontrolled.
conflicts: Sanger and Andrews emphasize Beecham's antiemetic discovery and its ondansetron-related patent; the 2004 court opinion describes a Glaxo pilot-based route and Glaxo's priority in a particular U.S. patent interference. These concern different activities and legal rights; this collection does not resolve all patent or scientific priority claims.

In the litigation, Teva argued that Fozard's earlier migraine publication disclosed a relevant antiemetic 5-HT3 link; the court rejected that interpretation. The underlying publication and testimony were not independently read to resolve that disclosure dispute.

The retrospective describes complete suppression in a passage citing a separate Miner, Sanger and Turner 1986 conference abstract; the read Miner and Sanger 1986 paper reports protection in three of four high-dose animals. The abstract was not read and the reports are not assumed to be the same experiment.
gaps: The trial exhibits, underlying 1985 migraine report, laboratory notebooks and complete patent file cited by the court were not separately examined.

The exact medicinal-chemistry route to ondansetron and precise priority among all early investigators were not established; the early Fozard migraine publication and underlying testimony in the litigation dispute were not read.
